X.originality: The culprit is her own tidy-wrapping habit (a cable tie she put on, matched to the spare on her lanyard), so the payoff is a character trait, not a gadget, and she re-commits it compulsively.
X.hook: Frame one shows the 1 cm gap and plants the guilty tie dead centre, so the problem is visible at once, though a medium locked-off shot reads less punchy than a macro.
X.coherence: Plant (tie in frame one), procedure, discovery, fix and re-offence connect causally, though it is a stretch that one cinched tie eats exactly the missing centimetre and re-tying pulls the seated plug out.
X.identity: Costume, glasses, warm disappointment, the rationed two-finger tap in S2 and the rule (she is the culprit, camera knows from frame one) all match the bible.
X.audiovisual: Every scene gives shot, lens, rig, motivated lighting with contact shadows, ambience, a specific foley list and captions, with no gaps.
X.feasibility: One 12-second continuous generation unit has to carry measuring, taping, crouching, snipping, re-tying and a matched end pose, which is a lot of fine hand action for one AI clip.
X.grounding: It keeps to every brief constraint (no dialogue, single location, zero cuts, loop, no readable text), and the why_send_it is tied to a concrete group-chat behaviour.
X.commercial_fit: No product category is mentioned; cable organisers would fit later without forcing, so it gets the default 3.

Y.originality: A clipboard lanyard snagging the drawer pull and dragging the table back is a fresh, physical, bible-tied way for her to undo her own fix.
Y.hook: It opens on a macro of the plug hovering 1 cm from the socket with the inspection-lamp beam locking onto the gap, which states the whole problem in one image.
Y.coherence: The causal chain is clear, but a plug 'hovering' mid-air on a taut cable, a lanyard dragging a heavy table, and an orange flag already on the cable before she arrives all strain the logic.
Y.identity: It fits the bible on costume, the single clipboard tap and 'the camera noticed; she did not', but the S2 handheld bob weakens the too-formal visual language.
Y.audiovisual: It gives detailed lens, rig, colour-bounce lighting, contact shadows, and foley per beat, plus a clean description of the loop transition.
Y.feasibility: The macro pull-back plus the precise lanyard-hook-drags-table interaction is hard to generate reliably, though the three short clips help.
Y.grounding: It respects the silent, single-location, cut and no-text constraints and has a plausible share rationale, but leaves the disclosure line empty.
Y.commercial_fit: No product category is mentioned, so it gets the default 3.

Z.originality: Committing the same fault with a second short cable is a direct but predictable mirror of the setup.
Z.hook: A low-angle macro of a dangling phone on a taut cable with a cable twang is a strong visible-problem opener.
Z.coherence: It never explains how plugging a torch into the socket drags the table away from the wall, and the premise block leaves out desire, obstacle and escalation.
Z.identity: A beige trench coat, tortoiseshell glasses and no aubergine jacket or chest lamp contradict the fixed bible silhouette, and the signature clipboard tap is missing.
Z.audiovisual: Shots, lighting and foley are given, but there is no rig, no voice field, no captions per scene, and the props lists are thin.
Z.feasibility: Three locked-off 4-second clips are simple to shoot, but the unclear table-drag mechanics would be hard to stage convincingly.
Z.grounding: It meets the brief's format constraints but drifts from the bible costume, and it has no share rationale tied to the objective.
Z.commercial_fit: No product category is mentioned, so it gets the default 3.

anti_template.evidence: Y and Z share the same skeleton (measure the gap, nudge the side table exactly 1 cm to fix it, then an object of hers drags the table back and pops the plug out), and only the trigger differs: lanyard snag versus torch cable.

notes: X is the only plan whose fault comes from a planted character habit visible in frame one, which fits the bible rule best, though its single 12-second generation unit is risky. Y has the strongest hook but shares a table-drag skeleton with Z, and Z also breaks the bible's fixed silhouette.
